newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge blames metal prices for poor Q3.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge blames metal prices for poor Q3.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd on Friday blamed poor metal prices for a drop in third-quarter earnings reported today.
Before extraordinary gains, the Toronto-based nickel giant earned C$30.1 million or C$0.17 a share, a steep drop from last year's third-quarter earnings of C$84.5 million or C$0.47 a share.

After extraordinary gains, the company reported profits of C$88.7 million or C$0.50 a share. The gains include C$101.5 million from a failed bid for Diamond Fields Resources and C$36.1 million from the issue of shares.
Third-quarter revenues fell to C$496.1 million from C$565.4 million in the year ago period.
Low copper prices cut into revenues from the Kidd Creek mine in Northern Ontario, the company said.
The decrease was partly offset by higher production and sales volumes at the company's operations in Sudbury, Ontario.
"This quarter was not expected to be a good quarter, with metal prices as they were," Wood Gundy analyst David Davidson said.
Copper has been in the doldrums since the Sumitomo scandal in June, while nickel prices have slid on poor demand.

Nickel production in Sudbury was near capacity for the quarter, but production of copper and precious metals failed to meet targets because of technical problems at the Nikkelwerk refinery in Norway, the company said.
Copper production at Kidd Creek was on target.
Ferronickel production was below capacity at the Dominican Republic operations because of lower grade feed and the downing of a power plant for maintenance.
In exploration, recent underground drilling at the Onaping deposit in Sudbury intersected 17.1 metres of 3.57 nickel and 1.89 percent copper.
At the Raglan project in Quebec, three new zones of mineralization were identified, the company said.
